tests/sort/sort-compress-proc.sh.note: Early-exit and pre-exec steps pass. The impatient-exit steps need -S 1k to spill a 10 KB input; XSH's run floor is 65536 bytes (sort.xsh buffered_sort). Lowering the floor to 4096 made the native compress tests (20000 lines, -S 10) exceed 2 minutes because the k-way merge of many runs is slow in XSH. Needs a faster run merge, then a GNU-sized floor.

tests/sort/sort-compress.sh.note: Same spill floor as sort-compress-proc: -S 1k on 2000 lines never writes temporary runs, so the gzip stand-in is never invoked (touch ok). The 'could not run compress program' diagnostic already matches.

tests/sort/sort-files0-from.sh.note: The extra-operand error now ends with the Try hint, as GNU prints. Native test test_sort_files0_from_extra_operand_has_usage_hint.

tests/sort/sort-float.sh.note: -g no longer treats values below double range as zero (3.36e-4932 sorts after 0 only when positive) and decides inf/nan from the text, so 1e400 stays finite. Native test test_sort_general_numeric_keeps_values_beyond_double_range_apart.

tests/sort/sort-merge.sh.note: nmerge-no is FIXED: the temp-directory error names the directory (test_sort_merge_temp_directory_failure_names_the_directory). The five batch-size cases (nmerge-0, nmerge-1, nmerge-neg, nmerge-nan, nmerge-big) expect a 'Try sort --help' line that util/gnu-patches/tests_sort_merge.pl.patch added; GNU 9.11 prints none, so XSH stays GNU-exact (wording-conflict).

tests/sort/sort-version.sh.note: sort -V now follows gnulib filevercmp: suffix split, '~' ordering, dot-name classes, and zero-run handling. Equal keys keep input order under --stable, --unique, and -r. Native tests test_sort_version_order_follows_filenvercmp and test_sort_version_unique_and_reverse_keep_equal_lines_in_input_order.

tests/uniq/uniq-c-width.sh.note: Exit 137: the test pipes up to 99999999 lines through yes | head | uniq -c. XSH uniq -c handles about 2 million lines in 95 seconds, so the run is killed. Needs a much faster line pipeline in the runtime.

tests/uniq/uniq.sh.note: All 66 stderr mismatches expect clap text (error: the argument ... cannot be used with ...; error: invalid value ...; For more information) from util/gnu-patches/error_msg_uniq.diff. GNU prints 'uniq: --group is mutually exclusive with -c/-d/-D/-u' and 'uniq: invalid argument 'badoption' for '--group'' with Valid arguments lists; XSH matches GNU (wording-conflict).

tests/comm/comm.sh.note: missing-arg1, missing-arg2, and extra-arg expect clap text, and delim-dual expects 'multiple conflicting output delimiters specified' (util/gnu-patches/tests_comm.pl.patch). GNU 9.12 src/comm.c and GNU 9.11 print 'comm: multiple output delimiters specified'; XSH matches GNU (wording-conflict).

tests/cut/cut-huge-range.sh.note: SKIP: get_min_ulimit_v_ probes RLIMIT_AS between 5 and 50 MB, and the XSH binary cannot start under that limit (thread creation fails with EAGAIN; it starts at about 90 MB). Needs a smaller runtime address-space footprint.

tests/cut/cut.sh.note: A zero range end is a decreasing range ('invalid decreasing range', as GNU prints for 2-0 and -0), while a zero start still reports 'fields are numbered from 1'. Native test test_cut_range_zero_start_and_decreasing_end_are_distinct_errors.

tests/expand/bounded-memory.sh.note: SKIP: get_min_ulimit_v_ finds no working limit below 50 MB, because the XSH runtime needs about 90 MB of address space. Same cause as cut-huge-range.

tests/expand/expand.sh.note: Tab-list errors (e1 through e7) print no 'Try' hint, as GNU does; they are reported by tab_error in core/lib/text_a2.xsh, which only expand and unexpand use. Native test test_expand_tab_list_errors_have_no_usage_hint.

tests/unexpand/bounded-memory.sh.note: SKIP: same address-space floor as expand/bounded-memory.

tests/unexpand/unexpand.sh.note: The obsolete -N form that overflows reports 'tab stop is too large' without the value, while -t N keeps the quoted value (GNU unexpand.c). Native test test_unexpand_obsolete_tab_stop_overflow_omits_the_value. Tab-list errors also lose the Try hint.

tests/fmt/long-line.sh.note: The default goal is width * 187 / 200 (GNU LEEWAY), and paragraphs are laid out in GNU's buffers of 998 words and 5000 word characters, with the flush cut and the previous line's length. Uniform spacing uses the final-sentence rule. Native test test_fmt_split_only_handles_a_paragraph_longer_than_one_buffer. Crown and tagged modes still keep the first continuation indent after a flush (GNU resets it), which no test covers.

tests/od/od-multiple-t.sh.note: Each -t column pads its fields to the widest block of all formats (GNU od.c width_per_block and pad_at), replacing the alignment estimate and its special case. Native test test_od_formats_share_one_block_width.

tests/numfmt/numfmt.sh.note: field-range-err-6 through -10 are FIXED (a repeated --field now fails with 'multiple field specifications'). Still failing: precision-large needs %.5119f, but Float.format caps precision at 100 in the runtime (XSH-GAP). neg-arg-not-option expects unquoted 'invalid option -- 9' from util/gnu-patches/tests_numfmt.patch; GNU quotes the option ('9'), so it is a wording-conflict.

tests/seq/seq-epipe.sh.note: SKIP: trap_sigpipe_or_skip_ needs 'yes' to print 'yes: standard output: Broken pipe' with SIGPIPE ignored (GNU does; core/yes.xsh does not). seq itself already prints 'seq: write error: Broken pipe' and exits 1. Needs the yes applet.

tests/seq/seq.sh.note: A width without the zero flag (seq -f %3.0f) pads with spaces; the zero-padding fast path now requires the zero flag or no width. Native assertion added to test_seq_format.

tests/printf/printf-cov.sh.note: printf with no operand prints 'printf: missing operand' with the Try hint and exits 1 (was exit 3). %c prints the first byte of the operand, not its numeric character (printf '%c' 65 prints '6'). Two native assertions that pinned the old behavior were corrected to GNU's output: test_printf_escapes_and_usage and test_printf_numeric_string_and_character_conversions.

tests/printf/printf-surprise.sh.note: SKIP: get_min_ulimit_v_ runs env under RLIMIT_AS and finds no limit below 50 MB; the XSH runtime needs about 90 MB. Same cause as cut-huge-range.

tests/factor/factor.sh.note: The z case expects clap text ('error: unexpected argument -1 found', tip, Usage) from util/gnu-patches/tests_factor_factor.pl.patch. The GNU ERR_SUBST keeps 'invalid option -- 1' and XSH matches it; passing requires clap wording (wording-conflict).
